subject.title: [Bug]: WEBUI / Edge cases —— Image input causes some multimodal models to misuse tool calling

question: Should OpenClaw preload explicit HTTP(S) image URLs from Web UI prompts into native vision input, and if so under what URL filtering, SSRF policy, timeout, and failure-reporting boundary?
rationale: The code fix is not only mechanical: it turns user prompt text into gateway outbound fetches, which affects privacy, SSRF controls, latency, and whether weak models should still see the fallback image tool.

options.title: Adopt narrow policy-bound preload
options.body: Preload only clear image URLs through existing remote-media SSRF policy and bounded timeouts, keep local/path rules intact, and require regression plus live Web UI proof before merge.

options.title: Keep native injection local-only
options.body: Leave HTTP(S) URLs as text/tool-driven input and solve the reported hallucinated tool calls by changing image-tool exposure or model guidance instead.

options.title: Defer to manual model/tool policy
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers decide whether weak model tool-calling should be handled by model routing, tool filtering, or media preload behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt narrow policy-bound preload
recommendation.body: Preload only clear image URLs through existing remote-media SSRF policy and bounded timeouts, keep local/path rules intact, and require regression plus live Web UI proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is tied to the original merge and later tightening of the native image injection boundary, and the remaining decision is a cross-cutting media safety/product boundary.
